summary: The study reports the first use of atomic layer deposition (ALD) to prepare ultrathin cobalt phosphide (Co-P) films. The process involves PH3 plasma as the phosphorus source and an additional H2 plasma step to remove excess phosphorus. The ALD process results in highly pure and smooth Co-P films with enhanced electrochemical and photoelectrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) activities compared to traditional post-phosphorization methods. The films can be conformally deposited on complex three-dimensional structures, highlighting their potential for applications in catalysis and energy storage.
evidence: The optimized ALD process followed the self-limited layer-by-layer growth behavior, and the deposited Co-P films were highly pure and smooth. The Co-P films deposited via ALD exhibited better electrochemical and photoelectrochemical hydrogen evolution reaction activities than similar Co-P films prepared by the traditional post-phosphorization method. Moreover, the deposition of ultrathin Co-P films on periodic trenches was demonstrated, which highlights the broad and promising potential application of this ALD process for a conformal coating of TMP films on complex three-dimensional (3D) architectures.
